title: 136. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Weighted Mean of Measurements
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the weighted mean of two measured values using given weights.
questions.question: A measurement of \(60\) has weight \(1\), and a measurement of \(90\) has weight \(2\). What is the weighted mean?
questions.explanation: The weighted mean is \(\frac{60\times 1+90\times 2}{1+2}=80\). The alternative \(75\) gives the two measurements equal weight.
questions.hint: Identify which weight belongs to each value.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the weighted mean when one measurement has a larger weight.
questions.question: A measurement of \(10\) has weight \(1\), and a measurement of \(20\) has weight \(3\). What is the weighted mean?
questions.explanation: The weighted mean is \(\frac{10\times 1+20\times 3}{1+3}=\frac{10+60}{4}=\frac{70}{4}=17.5\). Therefore, the weighted mean is \(17.5\). Option B is the unweighted mean.
questions.hint: Track both the weighted total and the total weight.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the weighted mean of three measured values.
questions.question: Three measurements are \(5\text{ kg}\) with weight \(3\), \(7\text{ kg}\) with weight \(2\), and \(9\text{ kg}\) with weight \(5\). What is the weighted mean?
questions.explanation: The weighted sum is \(5\times 3+7\times 2+9\times 5=15+14+45=74\). The total weight is \(3+2+5=10\). The weighted mean is \(\frac{74}{10}=7.4\text{ kg}\). Therefore, the correct value is \(7.4\text{ kg}\). The alternative is the unweighted arithmetic mean \(\frac{5+7+9}{3}=7.0\text{ kg}\).
questions.hint: Different group sizes should contribute different amounts to the combined total.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the weighted mean of three measured values with different weights.
questions.question: Measurements \(12\), \(15\), and \(18\) have weights \(2\), \(3\), and \(5\), respectively. What is the weighted mean?
questions.explanation: The weighted sum is \(12\times 2+15\times 3+18\times 5=24+45+90=159\). The total weight is \(2+3+5=10\). The weighted mean is \(\frac{159}{10}=15.9\). Therefore, the correct value is \(15.9\). The alternative is the unweighted arithmetic mean \(\frac{12+15+18}{3}=15\).
questions.hint: Identify which weight belongs to each value.

questions.concept: Finding a Missing Measurement from a Weighted Mean
questions.learningObjective: Determine a missing value when the weighted mean and weights are known.
questions.question: A value \(x\) has weight \(3\), and a value \(20\) has weight \(2\). The weighted mean is \(17\). What is \(x\)?
questions.explanation: The weighted mean satisfies \(\frac{3x+20\times 2}{3+2}=17\). Thus \(\frac{3x+40}{5}=17\), so \(3x+40=85\). Then \(3x=45\), and \(x=15\). Therefore, the missing value is \(15\). The alternative solves \(\frac{x+20}{2}=17\), treating the unequal weights as equal.
questions.hint: Track both the weighted total and the total weight.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate a weighted mean when the weights are given as percentages.
questions.question: A test score of \(70\) has weight \(25\%\), and a homework score of \(90\) has weight \(75\%\). What is the weighted mean score?
questions.explanation: The weighted score is \(0.25\times 70+0.75\times 90=85\). The alternative \(80\) is the unweighted arithmetic mean and ignores the stated weights.
questions.hint: Different group sizes should contribute different amounts to the combined total.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the weighted mean of three length measurements.
questions.question: Length measurements \(2.0\text{ m}\), \(3.0\text{ m}\), and \(5.0\text{ m}\) have weights \(1\), \(2\), and \(3\), respectively. What is the weighted mean length, rounded to two decimal places?
questions.explanation: The weighted sum is \(2.0\times 1+3.0\times 2+5.0\times 3=2.0+6.0+15.0=23.0\). The total weight is \(1+2+3=6\). The weighted mean is \(\frac{23.0}{6}=3.833\ldots\text{ m}\), which rounds to \(3.83\text{ m}\). Therefore, the correct value is \(3.83\text{ m}\). The alternative is the unweighted arithmetic mean \(\frac{2+3+5}{3}\approx 3.33\text{ m}\).
questions.hint: Identify which weight belongs to each value.

questions.concept: Combined Weighted Mean of Two Groups
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the overall weighted mean of two groups with different sizes.
questions.question: Group A has \(10\) measurements with mean \(70\). Group B has \(30\) measurements with mean \(80\). What is the overall weighted mean?
questions.explanation: The total for Group A is \(10\times 70=700\). The total for Group B is \(30\times 80=2{,}400\). The combined total is \(700+2{,}400=3{,}100\), and the total number of measurements is \(10+30=40\). The overall weighted mean is \(\frac{3{,}100}{40}=77.5\). Therefore, the correct value is \(77.5\). The alternative averages the group means without their sizes: \(\frac{70+80}{2}=75\).
questions.hint: Track both the weighted total and the total weight.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the weighted mean of three repeated measurements.
questions.question: Repeated measurements are \(10.0\text{ g}\) with weight \(1\), \(10.2\text{ g}\) with weight \(2\), and \(10.4\text{ g}\) with weight \(3\). What is the weighted mean mass, rounded to two decimal places?
questions.explanation: The weighted sum is \(10.0\times 1+10.2\times 2+10.4\times 3=10.0+20.4+31.2=61.6\). The total weight is \(1+2+3=6\). The weighted mean is \(\frac{61.6}{6}=10.266\ldots\text{ g}\), which rounds to \(10.27\text{ g}\). Therefore, the correct value is \(10.27\text{ g}\). The alternative is the unweighted arithmetic mean \(\frac{10.0+10.2+10.4}{3}=10.20\text{ g}\).
questions.hint: Different group sizes should contribute different amounts to the combined total.

questions.concept: Finding the Weight Ratio from a Weighted Mean
questions.learningObjective: Determine the ratio of weights when the weighted mean is known.
questions.question: The weighted mean of the values \(10\) and \(20\) is \(16\). What is the ratio of the weight of \(10\) to the weight of \(20\)?
questions.explanation: Let the weight of \(10\) be \(w_1\) and the weight of \(20\) be \(w_2\). Then \(\frac{10w_1+20w_2}{w_1+w_2}=16\). Multiplying gives \(10w_1+20w_2=16w_1+16w_2\), so \(4w_2=6w_1\), which simplifies to \(w_1:w_2=2:3\). Therefore, the ratio is \(2:3\). The alternative reverses the weight ratio. Weights in the ratio \(3:2\) would give \(\frac{10\times 3+20\times 2}{3+2}=14\), not the stated mean \(16\).
questions.hint: Identify which weight belongs to each value.
